newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to lend India $178 mln for refinery project.
newsitem.headline: Japan to lend India $178 mln for refinery project.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of Japan said on Wednesday it and the State Bank of India had signed a contract to lend the Indian bank $178 million for a refinery expansion project.

The loan is to be used by Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) to purchase plant facilities from Toyo Engineering Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp to boost output capacity at a refinery in the country's west coast city of Mangalore, an EX-Im Bank spokesman said.
The project, scheduled for completion by February 2000, will raise the refinery's annual production capacity by six million to nine million tonnes.

India's refining capacity has been falling behind its oil product demand, and gas oil demand in particular is likely to soar as trucks are expected to play a larger role in domestic distribution of goods, he said.
The refinery expansion is expected to put a curb on India's expenditures for oil product imports, he said.
